5.en: TRUE. Paragraph 2: 'all non-human creatures had been organized according to the categories of birds, beasts, or fish' — exactly three traditional groups.
5.uz: TRUE (To'g'ri). 2-bandda: 'barcha inson bo'lmagan mavjudotlar qushlar, hayvonlar yoki baliqlar toifalariga bo'lingan edi' — aniq uchta an'anaviy guruh.

6.en: NOT GIVEN. The passage discusses whether whales were classified as fish, but never states that fish themselves were seen as the 'lowest form of life'.
6.uz: NOT GIVEN (Berilmagan). Matnda kitlarning baliq sifatida tasniflanishi muhokama qilinadi, ammo baliqlarning o'zi 'hayotning eng past shakli' deb hisoblangani hech qachon aytilmagan.

7.en: FALSE. Paragraph 3 says the Linnaean system 'controversially classified whales as mammals' — whales were INCLUDED as mammals in this system, not excluded from it.
7.uz: FALSE (Noto'g'ri). 3-bandda Linney tizimi 'kitlarni sutemizuvchilar sifatida bahsli tarzda tasniflagani' aytiladi — kitlar bu tizimdan chiqarilmagan, aksincha sutemizuvchi sifatida KIRITILGAN.

8.en: Paragraph 4: Mitchill 'was a renowned natural history lecturer at the College of Physicians and Surgeons' — LECTURER is the missing word.
8.uz: 4-bandda: Mitchill 'Tibbiyot va jarrohlar kollejida tabiiy tarix bo'yicha taniqli MA'RUZACHI edi' — yetishmayotgan so'z LECTURER (ma'ruzachi).

9.en: Paragraph 5: Sampson asked 'plain-spoken WHALERS to make their case before the jury' — WHALERS is the missing word.
9.uz: 5-bandda: Sampson 'sodda so'zlovchi KIT OVCHILARDAN hakamlar oldida o'z dalillarini taqdim etishni' so'radi — yetishmayotgan so'z WHALERS (kit ovchilari).

10.en: Paragraph 6: Sampson claimed 'Mitchill's beliefs had their origin in EUROPE' — EUROPE is the missing word.
10.uz: 6-bandda: Sampson 'Mitchillning g'oyalari YEVROPADAN kelib chiqqan' deb da'vo qildi — yetishmayotgan so'z EUROPE (Yevropa).

11.en: Paragraph 6: 'In New York's markets, the MERCHANTS implicitly understood that whale oil and fish oil were not the same' — MERCHANTS is the missing word.
11.uz: 6-bandda: 'Nyu-York bozorlarida SAVDOGARLAR kit moyi va baliq moyi bir xil emasligini bilvosita tushunishgan' — yetishmayotgan so'z MERCHANTS (savdogarlar).

12.en: Paragraph 6: 'whale oil could be used as a FUEL for lamps because it could be burned without giving off smoke' — FUEL is the missing word.
12.uz: 6-bandda: 'kit moyi chiroqlar uchun YONILG'I sifatida ishlatilishi mumkin edi, chunki u tutunsiz yonadi' — yetishmayotgan so'z FUEL (yonilg'i).

13.en: Paragraph 7: 'Whether the issue today is the effects of human activity on the CLIMATE of this planet' — CLIMATE is the missing word.
13.uz: 7-bandda: 'Bugungi masala inson faoliyatining sayyoramiz IQLIMIGA ta'siri bo'lsa ham' — yetishmayotgan so'z CLIMATE (iqlim).

14.en: Paragraph A discusses packaging as 'a way to represent their brand and make consumers love their products' — 'Using packaging to communicate ideas and attract customers' (ix).
14.uz: A bandida o'rash 'brendni ifodalash va iste'molchilarni mahsulotni yoqtirishga undash usuli' sifatida muhokama qilinadi — 'G'oyalarni etkazish va xaridorlarni jalb qilish uchun o'ramdan foydalanish' (ix).

15.en: Paragraph B lists multiple consumer concerns driving change: 'sleek technology, reducing food waste, and minimizing health risks' — 'The many reasons for changes in packaging' (ii).
15.uz: B bandida o'zgarishlarni keltirib chiqaradigan bir qancha iste'molchi tashvishlari sanab o'tiladi: 'zamonaviy texnologiya, oziq-ovqat chiqindisini kamaytirish va sog'liq xavfini minimallashtirish' — 'O'ramdagi o'zgarishlarning ko'p sabablari' (ii).

16.en: Paragraph C is entirely about edible packaging (KFC's cup, Stonyfield's yogurt pearls) — 'Packaging that can be consumed with its contents' (iv).
16.uz: C bandi to'liq yeyiladigan o'ram haqida (KFC stakani, Stonyfield yogurt to'plari) — 'Tarkibi bilan birga iste'mol qilinishi mumkin bo'lgan o'ram' (i).

17.en: Paragraph D discusses Liquiglide letting all the sauce slide out, using more of the product — 'Packaging that allows consumers to use more of the product' (i).
17.uz: D bandida Liquiglide barcha souzni chiqarib yuborishga imkon berishi, mahsulotdan ko'proq foydalanish haqida — 'Iste'molchilarga mahsulotdan ko'proq foydalanish imkonini beradigan o'ram' (i).

18.en: Paragraph E discusses sell-by dates and 'active and intelligent' sensors to 'detect and later prevent food from spoiling' — 'Packaging that indicates when food is beginning to go rotten' (vii).
18.uz: E bandida sotish muddati va oziq-ovqatning buzilishini 'aniqlash va keyin oldini olish' uchun 'faol va aqlli' sensorlar muhokama qilinadi — 'Oziq-ovqat buzila boshlaganini ko'rsatadigan o'ram' (vii).

19.en: Paragraph F is entirely about disappearing/dissolving packaging — 'Packaging that vanishes or decomposes quickly' (x).
19.uz: F bandi to'liq yo'qoladigan/eriydigan o'ram haqida — 'Tezda yo'qoladigan yoki parchalanadigan o'ram' (x).

20.en: Paragraph G discusses compressed packaging for 'city dwellers who generally have tiny kitchens and no storage room' — 'Packaging that doesn't take up a lot of space' (v).
20.uz: G bandida 'odatda kichik oshxonasi va saqlash joyi yo'q shahar aholisi' uchun siqilgan o'ram muhokama qilinadi — 'Ko'p joy egallamaydigan o'ram' (v).

21.en: Paragraph C: 'KFC... is experimenting with an edible coffee-cup. Made from a hard cookie lined with heat-resistant white chocolate' — a sweet (cookie/chocolate) container for hot drinks, matching E.
21.uz: C bandida: 'KFC... yeyiladigan kofe chashkasi bilan tajriba o'tkazmoqda. Issiqlikka chidamli oq shokolad bilan qoplangan qattiq pechenedan tayyorlangan' — issiq ichimliklar uchun shirin (pechene/shokolad) idish, E ga mos.

22.en: Paragraph C: 'Loliware... introduced edible cupcake wrappers made from potato starch' — potato starch is a vegetable product, matching D.
22.uz: C bandida: 'Loliware... kartoshka kraxmalidan tayyorlangan yeyiladigan keks o'romlarini taqdim etdi' — kartoshka kraxmali sabzavot mahsuloti, D ga mos.

23.en: Paragraph G: 'Tomorrow Machine is also working on a compressed tiny package that expands into a full-size bowl when hot water is added' — gets bigger under certain conditions, matching A.
23.uz: G bandida: 'Tomorrow Machine issiq suv qo'shilganda to'liq o'lchamdagi piyolaga aylanadigan siqilgan kichik o'ram ustida ham ishlayapti' — ma'lum shartlarda kattalashadi, A ga mos.

24.en: Paragraph C: 'one decade-old edible invention continues to see great success — the clear PAPER used to wrap Japanese Botan Rice Candy' — PAPER is the missing word.
24.uz: C bandida: 'o'n yillik yeyiladigan ixtiro hamon katta muvaffaqiyatga ega — yapon Botan guruch konfetini o'raydigan shaffof QOG'OZ' — yetishmayotgan so'z PAPER (qog'oz).

25.en: Paragraph D: Liquiglide eliminates 'the 3 to 15 percent of SAUCES left inside traditional bottles' — SAUCES is the missing word.
25.uz: D bandida: Liquiglide an'anaviy shishalarda qolib ketgan '3-15 foiz SOUZNI' yo'q qiladi — yetishmayotgan so'z SAUCES (souzlar).

26.en: Paragraph F: Tomorrow Machine plans 'an oil bottle made from hardened SUGAR that cracks open like an egg' — SUGAR is the missing word.
26.uz: F bandida: Tomorrow Machine 'tuxum kabi yorilib ochiladigan qotgan SHAKARDAN tayyorlangan moy shishasini' rejalashtirmoqda — yetishmayotgan so'z SUGAR (shakar).

27.en: Paragraph D describes how Ed Cooke memorizes cards using a person-verb-object system, three cards at a time — a clear description of a complex memorization sequence.
27.uz: D bandida Ed Cookening odam-fe'l-buyum tizimi yordamida, har safar uch kartadan kartalarni qanday yodlashi tasvirlangan — bu murakkab yodlash ketma-ketligining aniq tasviri.

28.en: Paragraph G: 'During two years of experimentation, S.V. increased his ability to recall numbers from seven to over eighty' — a clear example of memory improving over time.
28.uz: G bandida: 'Ikki yillik tajriba davomida S.V. raqamlarni yodlash qobiliyatini yettidan sakson dan ortiqga oshirdi' — vaqt o'tishi bilan xotira yaxshilanishining aniq misoli.

29.en: Paragraph A describes '34 contestants gathered at the World Memory Championships' at Oxford — a description of the competition itself.
29.uz: A bandida Oxford universitetida 'Jahon Xotira Chempionatida 34 ishtirokchi yig'ilgani' tasvirlangan — bu musobaqaning o'zi haqidagi tasvir.

30.en: Paragraph E: 'The term photographic memory... most researchers agree there is no proof that such a memory truly exists' — a popular belief that experts say is unproven.
30.uz: E bandida: 'fotografik xotira atamasi... ko'pchilik tadqiqotchilar bunday xotira haqiqatan mavjudligiga dalil yo'q deb kelishadi' — mutaxassislar isbotlanmagan deb hisoblaydigan ommabop ishonch.

31.en: Paragraph B: 'the loci method, reportedly originating in 477 BC with the Greek poet Simonides of Ceos' — the first recorded use of location-based memorizing.
31.uz: B bandida: 'loci usuli, taxminan miloddan avvalgi 477-yilda yunon shoiri Simonides tomonidan boshlangan' — joylashuvga asoslangan yodlashning birinchi qayd etilgan ishlatilishi.

32.en: Paragraph F: Shereshevski 'experienced synesthesia, a rare sensory condition where the senses are interconnected, which significantly improved his memorization ability' — an unusual condition improving memory.
32.uz: F bandida: Shereshevski 'sinesteziyani boshdan kechirdi, bu sezgilar bir-biriga bog'langan kamdan-kam uchraydigan holat bo'lib, uning yodlash qobiliyatini sezilarli darajada yaxshilagan' — xotirani yaxshilaydigan g'ayrioddiy holat.

33.en: Paragraph D: 'Ed Cooke has memorized a SPECIFIC HUMAN BEING, verb, and object that he associates with every card' — SPECIFIC HUMAN BEING is the missing phrase.
33.uz: D bandida: 'Ed Cooke har bir karta bilan bog'liq BELGILI INSON, fe'l va buyumni yodlab olgan' — yetishmayotgan ibora SPECIFIC HUMAN BEING (belgili inson).

34.en: Paragraph D: 'he does it THREE CARDS in one go, with every three-card group forming a composite picture' — THREE CARDS is the missing phrase.
34.uz: D bandida: 'u buni bir vaqtning o'zida UCH KARTA bilan amalga oshiradi, har uch kartali guruh murakkab tasvir hosil qiladi' — yetishmayotgan ibora THREE CARDS (uch karta).

35.en: Paragraph D: 'He then places those images along a SPECIFIC FAMILIAR PATH in his mind' — SPECIFIC FAMILIAR PATH is the missing phrase.
35.uz: D bandida: 'U keyin bu tasvirlarni o'z ongida BELGILI TANISH YO'L bo'ylab joylashtiradi' — yetishmayotgan ibora SPECIFIC FAMILIAR PATH (belgili tanish yo'l).

36.en: Paragraph D: 'Cooke takes a MENTAL WALK along his route and translates the images into cards' — MENTAL WALK is the missing phrase.
36.uz: D bandida: 'Cooke o'z yo'li bo'ylab AQLIY SAYR qiladi va tasvirlarni kartalarga aylantiradi' — yetishmayotgan ibora MENTAL WALK (aqliy sayr).

37.en: Paragraph C: researchers 'found that the memory champions were activating some brain regions... known to be involved in visual memory and spatial navigation' — matching B.
37.uz: C bandida: tadqiqotchilar 'xotira chempionlari... vizual xotira va fazoviy yo'l topish bilan bog'liq miya hududlarini faollashtirayotganini' aniqladilar — B ga mos.

38.en: Paragraph B: after Simonides's discovery, 'the loci method became widely embraced across ancient Greece... incorporated into educational curricula... cornerstone of rhetorical training' — matching C (widespread for memorizing speeches).
38.uz: B bandida: Simonides kashfiyotidan keyin, 'loci usuli qadimgi Gretsiyada keng qabul qilindi... ta'lim dasturlariga kiritildi... notiqlik mashg'ulotlarining asosi bo'ldi' — C ga mos (nutq va matnlarni yodlash uchun keng tarqalgan).

39.en: Paragraph G: 'naturals exhibit strong memory across many types of tasks and can retain those memories more easily' — naturals are better at retaining a WIDE VARIETY of tasks, matching E.
39.uz: G bandida: 'tabiiy xotira sohiblari ko'plab turdagi vazifalarda kuchli xotira namoyish etadi va bu xotiralarni osonroq saqlab qoladi' — tabiiy xotira sohiblari TURLI-TUMAN vazifalarni saqlashda yaxshiroq, E ga mos.

40.en: Paragraph G: Ericsson 'discovered that their remarkable abilities were actually based on the use of specific techniques — sometimes unconsciously — combined with extensive practice' when he reviewed Shereshevski's case — matching D, not the synesthesia explanation in Paragraph F.
40.uz: G bandida: Ericsson Shereshevski holatini qayta ko'rib chiqqanda 'ularning ajoyib qobiliyatlari aslida ba'zan ongsiz ravishda qo'llaniladigan maxsus usullar va keng amaliyot natijasi ekanligini' aniqladi — bu D ga mos, F banddagi sinesteziya tushuntirishiga emas.

1.en: Paragraph A says the best-known celluloid product was 'photographic film' — this directly completes the table's 'common uses' column.
1.uz: A bandida aytilishicha, sellyuloiddan tayyorlangan eng mashhur mahsulot — 'fotografik plyonka' (photographic film) bo'lgan. Bu jadvaldagi 'ishlatilishi' ustunini to'g'ridan-to'g'ri to'ldiradi.

2.en: Paragraph B states 'Baekeland called it Bakelite' — this is the name of the plastic invented in 1907.
2.uz: B bandida 'Baekeland uni Bakelite deb atadi' deyilgan — bu 1907-yilda ixtiro qilingan plastik moddaning nomi.

3.en: Paragraph B says Bakelite 'was soon being used in the manufacture of electrical switches' due to its insulating properties.
3.uz: B bandida Bakelite o'zining izolyatsiya xususiyati tufayli 'elektr o'tkazgichlarni (switches) ishlab chiqarishda' ishlatilgani aytilgan.

4.en: Paragraph C states 'in the 1930s, chemists in Britain discovered' how to make polythene — so the country of origin is Britain.
4.uz: C bandida '1930-yillarda Britaniyalik kimyogarlar' polietilenni qanday yasashni kashf etganlari aytilgan — demak, kelib chiqish davlati Britaniya.

5.en: The passage describes PVC as 'a fireproof plastic suitable for drains and gutters' — fireproof is the missing property.
5.uz: Matnda PVC haqida 'yong'inga chidamli (fireproof), drenaj quvurlari uchun mos plastik' deyilgan — fireproof yetishmayotgan xususiyat.

6.en: Paragraph D opens with 'Polystyrene, a hard, clear material like glass' — so polystyrene resembles glass.
6.uz: D bandi 'Polistirol, shisha kabi qattiq va tiniq material' so'zlari bilan boshlanadi — demak, polistirol shishaga o'xshaydi (resembles glass).

7.en: Paragraph D says polyurethane 'was commonly produced as a foam' — foam is the correct answer.
7.uz: D bandida poliuretan 'odatda ko'pik (foam) shaklida ishlab chiqarilgan' deyilgan — to'g'ri javob foam.

8.en: FALSE. Paragraph A explains rubber IS a polymer made of repeating bonded units — the same principle (polymerization) underlies plastics too, so the structures are related, not 'very different'.
8.uz: FALSE (Noto'g'ri). A bandida tushuntirilishicha, kauchuk AYNAN polimer bo'lib, takrorlanuvchi birikkan birliklardan iborat — xuddi shu tamoyil (polimerizatsiya) plastmassalar uchun ham asos bo'ladi. Demak, tuzilishlar bir-biriga juda farqli emas, aksincha o'xshash.

9.en: NOT GIVEN. The passage only says Hyatt won the prize with celluloid — it never states his profession or whether he was an industrial chemist.
9.uz: NOT GIVEN (Berilmagan). Matnda faqat Hyatt sellyuloid bilan mukofotni yutgani aytilgan — uning kasbi yoki sanoat kimyogari bo'lgan-bo'lmaganligi haqida hech narsa aytilmagan.

10.en: FALSE. Celluloid is a thermoplastic (can be softened and reshaped by heat repeatedly), while Bakelite is a thermoset (cannot be softened once set) — they react oppositely to heat.
10.uz: FALSE (Noto'g'ri). Sellyuloid termoplastik (issiqlik bilan qayta-qayta yumshatilishi mumkin), Bakelite esa termoset (qattiqlashgandan keyin yumshamaydi) — ular issiqlikka qarama-qarshi ta'sir ko'rsatadi.

11.en: TRUE. Paragraph F states recycling is difficult 'as different types of plastic are often found in the same items and call for different treatments' — exactly matching the statement.
11.uz: TRUE (To'g'ri). F bandida aytilishicha, qayta ishlash qiyin, chunki 'bir xil buyumda turli xil plastik turlari uchraydi va ularning har biri boshqacha ishlov talab qiladi' — bu bayonotga to'liq mos keladi.

12.en: FALSE. Paragraph G says starch makes plastic biodegradable because bacteria attack it and cause it to 'fall apart' — this is the opposite of making it 'more durable'.
12.uz: FALSE (Noto'g'ri). G bandida kraxmal plastikni biologik chiriydigan qiladi, chunki bakteriyalar unga ta'sir qilib, uni 'parchalab yuboradi' deyilgan — bu 'chidamliroq qilish'ga teskari holat.

13.en: TRUE. The passage explicitly says light-decaying plastic bottles 'have to be stored in the dark' to prevent early disintegration — this matches 'particular storage conditions'.
13.uz: TRUE (To'g'ri). Matnda aniq aytilgan: yorug'lik ta'sirida chiriydigan plastik shishalar erta parchalanib ketmasligi uchun 'qorong'ida saqlanishi kerak' — bu 'maxsus saqlash sharoitlari'ga mos keladi.

14.en: Paragraph F describes Doug Heath's 12-year breeding project that produced disease-resistant tomatoes — this is the 'research aimed at restoring health'.
14.uz: F bandida Doug Heath ning 12 yillik seleksiya loyihasi tasvirlangan, u kasalliklarga chidamli pomidorlar yaratdi — bu 'sog'ligini tiklashga qaratilgan tadqiqot'.

15.en: Paragraph A introduces and then debunks the 'myth' that heirlooms have superior diversity/genes — this is the 'false belief' referred to.
15.uz: A bandi meros pomidorlarning gen xilma-xilligi ustunroq degan 'afsona'ni keltiradi va keyin uni rad etadi — bu 'noto'g'ri ishonch'ga ishora.

16.en: Paragraph E discusses how heirloom flavour depends on plant productivity (fewer fruits = more flavour) rather than genes — this describes the flavour.
16.uz: E bandida meros pomidor mazasi genlarga emas, balki o'simlik unumdorligiga bog'liqligi tushuntirilgan (kamroq meva = ko'proq mazali) — bu mazani tasvirlaydi.

17.en: Paragraph D mentions the gene that 'increases fruit size by 50 percent' — 'probably the most important event in domestication', matching 'a single gene that significantly improves cultivation'.
17.uz: D bandida 'mevani 50 foizga kattalashtiradigan' gen tilga olinadi — bu 'domestikatsiyadagi eng muhim voqea', ya'ni 'yetishtirishni sezilarli darajada yaxshilaydigan bitta gen'ga mos.

18.en: Paragraph D: Esther van der Knaap (B) 'took a gene from one heirloom tomato and inserted it into a wild relative' and the fruit 'became shaped like pears' — a clear shape change from gene transplant.
18.uz: D bandida: Esther van der Knaap (B) 'bir meros pomidordan gen olib, uni yovvoyi qarindosh pomidorga ko'chirdi' va meva 'noksimon shaklga aylandi' — gen ko'chirish orqali shaklning aniq o'zgarishi.

19.en: Paragraph E: Roger Chetelat (C) explains heirlooms' taste 'may have less to do with genes than with the productivity of the plant and the growing environment' — directly matches the statement about yield/cultivation.
19.uz: E bandida: Roger Chetelat (C) meros pomidorlarning mazasi 'genlarga emas, balki o'simlik unumdorligi va o'stirish muhitiga' bog'liq ekanligini tushuntiradi — bu hosildorlik/yetishtirish haqidagi bayonotga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri mos keladi.

20.en: Paragraph F: Doug Heath (D) created a tomato 'less prone to cracking' with 12 disease-resistant genes, while claiming to 'maintain a comparable flavor and sugar profile' — stronger AND equally tasty.
20.uz: F bandida: Doug Heath (D) yorilishga kamroq moyil, 12 ta kasallikka chidamli genga ega pomidor yaratdi, shu bilan birga 'mos keladigan ta'm va shakar darajasini saqlab qolish'ni da'vo qildi — kuchliroq HAM xuddi shunday mazali.

21.en: Paragraph A: Steven Tanksley (A) states 'There're probably no more than 10 mutant genes that create the diversity of heirlooms you see' — directly matches the statement.
21.uz: A bandida: Steven Tanksley (A) 'ko'rinadigan xilma-xillikni yaratadigan 10 tadan ko'p bo'lmagan mutant gen bor, ehtimol' deydi — bu bayonotga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri mos keladi.

22.en: The text says 'whereas scientists have uncovered a wealth of archaeological evidence on early farming practices... the record is blank when it comes to the tomato' — ARCHAEOLOGICAL is the missing word.
22.uz: Matnda 'olimlar boshqa ekinlar bo'yicha ko'p arxeologik dalillarni topgan bo'lsalar-da... pomidor bo'yicha bunday yozuvlar yo'q' deyilgan — yetishmayotgan so'z ARCHAEOLOGICAL (arxeologik).

23.en: The text states 'the modern tomato seems to have its origins in the Andes in South America' — ANDES is the missing word.
23.uz: Matnda 'zamonaviy pomidor Janubiy Amerikadagi Andlardan kelib chiqgan ko'rinadi' deyilgan — yetishmayotgan so'z ANDES.

24.en: The text says 'the closest relative is the currant tomato which... split from today's tomato some 1.4 million years ago' — CURRANT is the missing word.
24.uz: Matnda 'eng yaqin qarindosh — currant pomidori, u zamonaviy pomidordan 1.4 million yil oldin ajralgan' deyilgan — yetishmayotgan so'z CURRANT.

25.en: The text says 'this mutation, which enlarges tomatoes by producing compartments known as locules' — MUTATION is the missing word.
25.uz: Matnda 'locules deb ataladigan bo'shliqlar hosil qilib pomidorlarni kattalashtiradigan mutatsiya' deyilgan — yetishmayotgan so'z MUTATION.

26.en: The text says heirlooms 'often suffer from infections that cause the fruit to crack, split and otherwise rot quickly' — INFECTIONS is the missing word.
26.uz: Matnda meros pomidorlar 'ko'pincha mevani yorilishi, bo'linishi va tezda chirishiga olib keladigan infeksiyalardan aziyat chekadi' deyilgan — yetishmayotgan so'z INFECTIONS.

27.en: Paragraph D: studies 'sought relationships between the degree of attention... and the amount they subsequently appeared to have LEARNT' — option D.
27.uz: D bandida: tadqiqotlar 'bolalarning diqqat darajasi va keyinchalik ular o'rgangan miqdor o'rtasidagi bog'liqlikni' qidirdi — bu D (learning/o'rganish) variantiga mos.

28.en: Paragraph D: observation was used 'to assess teachers' COMPETENCE and allocate merit payments' — option B.
28.uz: D bandida: kuzatish 'o'qituvchilarning kompetensiyasini baholash va mukofot to'lovlarini ajratish' uchun ishlatilgan — bu B (competence/kompetensiya) variantiga mos.

29.en: Paragraph E: the shift was 'partly the emergence of totalitarian regimes... led to a shift... towards a scrutiny of AUTHORITARIANISM itself' — option A.
29.uz: E bandida: o'zgarish 'totalitar rejimlarning paydo bo'lishi... avtoritarizmning o'ziga sinchkov nazar tashlashga olib keldi' — bu A (authoritarianism/avtoritarizm) variantiga mos.

30.en: Paragraph E: investigators examined the 'PROCESSES taking place within small discussion groups' — option G.
30.uz: E bandida: tadqiqotchilar 'kichik munozara guruhlarida sodir bo'layotgan jarayonlarni' o'rgandilar — bu G (processes/jarayonlar) variantiga mos.

31.en: Paragraph H: Withall's analysis 'concentrated... on the study of teachers' VERBAL BEHAVIOR' — option J.
31.uz: H bandida: Withallning tahlili 'o'qituvchilarning og'zaki xulq-atvorini o'rganishga' qaratilgan edi — bu J (verbal behavior/og'zaki xulq-atvor) variantiga mos.

32.en: Paragraph H: Withall 'made efforts towards increasing the RELIABILITY of analyses' — option H.
32.uz: H bandida: Withall 'tahlillarning ishonchliligini oshirishga harakat qildi' — bu H (reliability/ishonchlilik) variantiga mos.

33.en: Paragraph I: the 1960-70 decade 'produced a large number of studies of classroom processes, based on OBSERVATION of teachers at work' — option E.
33.uz: I bandida: 1960-70 yillarda 'o'qituvchilarni ish vaqtida kuzatishga asoslangan' ko'plab tadqiqotlar o'tkazildi — bu E (observation/kuzatish) variantiga mos.

34.en: Paragraph B: 'Rostker concluded that the intelligence of the teacher is the most important single factor conditioning teaching ability' — this is Rostker (B), not Rolfe.
34.uz: B bandida: 'Rostker o'qituvchining aqlliligi o'qitish qobiliyatining eng muhim yagona omili ekanligini xulosa qildi' — bu Rostker (B), Rolfe emas.

35.en: Paragraph G: 'Lewin, Lippitt and White... studied the effects of different teaching styles. They arranged for three groups of five boys each to be taught in very different ways' — this is the experiment described.
35.uz: G bandida: 'Lewin, Lippitt va White... turli o'qitish uslublarining ta'sirini o'rgandilar. Ular har biri besh boladan iborat uch guruhni har xil usulda o'qitishni tashkil qildilar' — bu tasvirlangan tajriba.

36.en: Paragraph C: 'Stevens made 100 random observations of lessons... in order to analyze the number and nature of QUESTIONS being asked by teachers' — this matches Stevens (E).
36.uz: C bandida: 'Stevens darslarning 100 tasodifiy kuzatishini o'tkazdi... o'qituvchilar so'raydigan savollarning soni va tabiatini tahlil qilish uchun' — bu Stevens (E)ga mos.

37.en: Paragraph B: 'Rolfe... found no correlation between intelligence and teaching efficiency: he claimed that the teacher's PERSONALITY was what produced good teaching' — this is Rolfe (C).
37.uz: B bandida: 'Rolfe... aql va o'qitish samaradorligi orasida bog'liqlik topmadi: u o'qituvchining shaxsiyati yaxshi o'qitishni ta'minlaydi deb da'vo qildi' — bu Rolfe (C).

38.en: Paragraph E discusses how 'the emergence of totalitarian regimes in Europe' (a political event) shifted research interest — this is the paragraph about political influence.
38.uz: E bandida 'Yevropada totalitar rejimlarning paydo bo'lishi' (siyosiy voqea) tadqiqot qiziqishini qanday o'zgartirgani muhokama qilinadi — bu siyosiy ta'sir haqidagi band.

39.en: Paragraph F describes Anderson's specific categories: 'Dominative acts by children included blaming and snatching toys... integrative acts included sharing facilities' — a clear example of behavior categorization.
39.uz: F bandida Andersonning aniq toifalari tasvirlangan: 'Bolalarning hukmronlik xatti-harakatlariga ayblash va o'yinchoqlarni tortib olish kirgan... integratsion xatti-harakatlarga imkoniyatlarni baham ko'rish kirgan' — xulq-atvorni tasniflashning aniq namunasi.

40.en: Paragraph D explains that because 'formal' teaching with factual recall was the norm, researchers naturally focused on 'attentiveness' — this is the stated reason for studying children's attention.
40.uz: D bandida tushuntirilishicha, faktlarni yodlashga asoslangan 'rasmiy' o'qitish me'yor bo'lgani uchun, tadqiqotchilar tabiiy ravishda 'diqqatlilik'ga e'tibor qaratdilar — bu bolalar diqqatini o'rganishning aytilgan sababi.
